public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's $11 billion round will not cover even one quarter of its compute costs.

statement.excerpt: In other words, that $11 billion round won’t even cover a quarter of OpenAI’s compute costs, and it’s fair to ask both why this round had to close right now and what exactly the company does going forward.

our_interpretation: A quarter means three months, rather than one-fourth of an unspecified total.
This is a comparison with current spending, not a forecast about a specified future quarter.
Use July 1 through September 30, 2026, the latest completed quarter before the post and the period corresponding to the context's latest Microsoft fiscal quarter.
Compute costs include training and inference across suppliers. Broader research expenses, revenue-sharing payments and future commitments are not interchangeable with compute expenditure.
The estimate basis reflects the speaker's inference from press-reported expenses and supplier disclosures.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that OpenAI incurred more than USD 11 billion in compute costs during the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that OpenAI incurred USD 11 billion or less in compute costs during the target quarter.
